merge.label: Merge rules (two profiles of one person)
merge.help: Which matches put two customer profiles on the "To review" list as maybe the same person: the same e-mail, one profile's WhatsApp number being the other's phone, the same name with the same address, or the same identity in the order identity graph (only while that graph is on in Orders › Risk rules). The shop never merges by itself: a person with the merge permission looks at both and presses Merge, or "Not the same person" (then the pair is never suggested again). A merge moves nothing — orders, wallets and notes stay where they are and the first profile's page shows both — and "Split" undoes it exactly. "Per page": how many pairs the list shows at a time. "Note needed": a merge needs a short note (a split always does). Off ("Suggest pairs" off): no suggestions; a person can still merge two profiles by hand.

phoneMask.label: Masked phone numbers
phoneMask.help: A team member without the "full phone number" permission sees customers' numbers masked, with this many digits kept at the start and at the end (3 and 3: 017•••••678). With the permission (you have every permission) the number is shown in full, and every copy and call is logged in "Who looked at this customer".

list.label: Customers list and its views
list.help: How many customers one page of the Customers list shows; how many orders make a customer "Returning" (fewer is "New"); after how many days without an order a customer who already had a delivery shows under "At risk"; and the delivered spend (Sales, delivered orders only) that makes a customer "VIP". The VIP figure is empty as it ships: the VIP view stays hidden until you type your own figure. Nothing here changes a price, COD or an offer; the views only sort who is who.

profile.label: One customer's page
profile.help: How many orders one customer's page lists before "Older"; how many exchanges and support conversations each of its lists shows; and how many lines of "Who looked at this customer" (every open of the page and every copy or call of the full number, with who and when) the owner sees there (0 hides the card; the full log stays). Nothing here changes what is recorded.

segments.label: Saved segments
segments.help: Groups of customers by what they really did (orders, delivered spend, true delivery share, last order, a category or size bought, an area, where they first came from, offers consent, a refusal, an exchange), saved by name and used again in the Customers list and later in campaigns. "On": the Segments page counts and saves; off (as shipped): the page only says it is off. "Most segments": how many saved segments the store may keep (archived ones do not count). "Most conditions": how many conditions one segment joins with “and”. "Shown in the builder": how many matching customers the builder lists beside its live count. A segment never sends anything by itself, and nothing in it moves money or blocks anyone.

journey.label: Customer journey view
journey.help: The Journey tab on a customer's page: every touch of that person in order, newest first — each profile and where it came from, his visits to the site (grouped by browsing session), touches like an ad click or a chat start, every order with its channel and campaign and how it ended, exchanges, messages sent to him, support conversations, reviews, wallet credits and debits (only for those who may see money), consent changes, merges and staff notes. "How he first came" is the earliest touch with a source or a campaign. Off (as shipped): the tab says it is off. "Kinds": which touches are listed. "Per page": rows before "Older". Nothing new is stored and no phone number is shown in a row.

journeys.label: Automations (customer journeys)
journeys.help: Journeys that start on a trigger (days after a delivered order: the product-life reminder; days without an order; days after joining), then wait, check and send a message. Off as shipped; each message needs the customer's yes for offers.

email.label: E-mail marketing
email.help: Offer e-mails from your own templates to a saved segment (Messages › E-mail), with the delivery log. Off as shipped. Each e-mail goes only to a customer who said yes to offer e-mails and always carries the unsubscribe line. "Per person a week": the most such e-mails one person gets in seven days. "Per run": how many people one run queues (the throttle). Open and click tracking are each off until you turn them on. "Result days": orders a receiver places within these days count as the send's result (Sales only when delivered).

aiWriter.label: AI campaign writer
aiWriter.help: Two or three versions of an offer e-mail in your own voice, from what you say the message is about (Messages › E-mail, "Write with AI"). Off as shipped; it also needs AI for the whole shop. Until an AI provider is connected the practice writer only joins your own words. "Greeting", "Sign-off" and "How you talk" are your words in each language. "Longest SMS" is the most characters an SMS draft may have. A draft only fills the form: you pick one, change it, save it and send it yourself.

sendAdvice.label: Who and when to send
sendAdvice.help: On an e-mail send: your saved segments ranked by how many of their people bought in the last days (and can get offer e-mails), and the hours and weekday your orders come in, outside the quiet hours — each with the numbers behind it. Off as shipped. Works on your own data without AI. "Days to look back": how far back orders are read. "Fewest orders": below this the timing advice waits. "Hours in the window": how wide the suggested sending window is. "Segments shown": how many are suggested. Advice only: you pick.

points.label: Rewards and points
points.help: Points for each delivered order, by your own rule: "Points per ৳100" of the goods (the delivery charge never counts) and/or "Points per order". Points are given "Days to wait" after the delivery (the exchange window) and never for an order delivered more than "Days to look back" before. Turning points into money is yours too: each block of "Points to turn in" becomes "Wallet credit" in the customer's wallet, and only when both are set. Off as shipped with every number at 0. "Per run": how many orders one run reads. The late-delivery apology credit is under Money › Wallet.

export.label: Customer export
export.help: Off as shipped. When on, a person holding "Export customers" downloads the list's people (the view, search and filters on screen) as one CSV file, after typing why; the reason, the person and the count are logged. "Most people in one file": more are refused with the count, never cut. The retention rule always applies: a customer who asked to be forgotten, or an archived profile, is never in the file; the address, IP and location never; the phone number only as the person may see it.

winback.label: Win-back campaigns
winback.help: A message to the people who have stopped ordering (Messages › Campaigns): an SMS or WhatsApp from one of your own templates to those whose last order is older than the days you set. Off as shipped. Nothing goes until a person with the send right schedules a campaign. Each message is an offer: only to customers who said yes to offers on that channel, never in the quiet hours. "Offers by phone in 7 days": the most offers (automations and campaigns together) one person gets in a week. "Days between win-backs": nobody gets a second win-back sooner. "Per run": how many people one run queues. "Days for results": orders within these days of the message count for it. "First "no order for" days": what a new campaign starts with. A campaign never makes an offer or a discount: it only sends your words. "Stop line": added to every campaign SMS so a customer can say no to offers.

birthday.label: Birthday field
birthday.help: Off as shipped. When on, My account › Profile has a small "Birthday" box: a signed-in customer may give the day and the month (the year only when "Ask for the year" is on), change it or clear it, and his customer page shows it. Nothing is sent or given for it: birthday wishes and gifts are a separate module that stays parked until you ask for it. Erasing a customer clears it.

report.label: Customer report
report.help: Off as shipped. When on, Reports › Customers shows, for a period you pick, how many people bought for the first time, how many came back, how many have gone quiet and the repeat rate, overall and for each saved segment (segments need their own switch). "Quiet after": a buyer with no order for this many days, and none in the period, counts as quiet (churned). "Segments in the report": how many saved segments it splits by, newest first. It only counts: nothing is sent or changed, and no money figure is shown.

approvalHistory.label: Customer history at approval
approvalHistory.help: Off as shipped. When on, Orders › To confirm shows the caller a summary of the customer's earlier orders under the same number before he confirms: orders, true deliveries (a delivery still being checked is not counted), refusals at the door and charge-paid returns with their reasons, returns after delivery, exchanges and cancels. A refusal the shop caused is shown and never counted. It only shows: it never confirms, holds or blocks.

grades.label: Customer grading
grades.help: Off as shipped, with no grade made for you. When on, the team sees each customer's grade — one of your own grades, each with its rule of true deliveries and refusals that were not the shop's fault — as a small mark on the customer list, the customer's page and Orders › To confirm, and a "Verified" mark once he has the true deliveries you set (0 = no mark). A customer gets the highest grade (in your order) whose rule he meets. "Good customer from": a grade at or above it also counts as a good customer for the fraud check's good-customer override, which has its own switch (Orders › Risk rules › Good customer). A grade is only shown to the team: it never blocks anyone, never holds an order and never changes cash on delivery.
